content: Uptime Kuma (self-hosted, unlimited monitors, free) is best for 'is it reachable' checks — HTTP(S)/TCP/DNS probing with a status dashboard and notifications (Telegram/email/Discord/webhook); mimics what a browser experiences. Healthchecks.io (or self-hosted healthchecks) is a dead-man's-switch for cron jobs (e.g. the nightly SQLite backup) — your script pings a URL on success, and you get alerted if the ping is late/missing, catching silent failures that uptime pings can't. For a single Pi hobby deployment, common pattern: run Uptime Kuma as a lightweight container/process elsewhere (not on the same Pi, so it can detect the Pi being fully down) for external reachability checks, plus a Healthchecks.io free-tier ping for the backup cron — zero cost.
